fact_check.claim: Bitcoin went from $84,500 to $87,200 in 15 hours, $216M in shorts liquidated; it reversed one hour after the jobs data and dropped $3,100, wiping out $270M of longs in five hours (transcript, a post Mike read on stream)

CoinGlass 24h liquidations: $433.57M total, longs $321.77M (74.2%), shorts $111.80M. $BTC $84,886 on 2026-10-03. fact_check.claim: Employment data came in weaker than expected, which lowers the chance of a Fed rate hike at the end of October; 'we are going to get a pause' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and numbers added: September nonfarm payrolls +29K against forecasts of 84K to 90K, unemployment rate 4.2% (BLS, Oct 2, 2026). Prediction markets on Oct 3: 82% hold on Oct 28, hike about 18% (Kalshi 18.5%, Polymarket 17.5%), up from about 65% hold on Sept 30 (uptober plan). Copy: '29K against about 90K expected', 'about an 82% chance the Fed holds rates on Oct 28'. The 'another hike' / 'hike cycle' wording is not used.

fact_check.claim: ISM PMI: expectation 55, September 54.5, prior 54.6; the index sat below 50 for four or five years for the first time since 1948, broke above 50 in January of this year, and is now growing slowly instead of shooting up; a parabolic bull run needs it above 60 (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: figures verified: September 2026 Manufacturing PMI 54.5 vs 55.0 expected, August 54.6 (released Oct 1), the ninth consecutive month of expansion; January 2026 printed 52.6, the first expansion in 12 months. The pre-2026 history is CORRECTED: 26 straight months of contraction through Dec 2024, two months above 50 (Jan and Feb 2025), then contraction for the rest of 2025, so about 36 of the 38 months from Nov 2022 to Dec 2025 were under 50. Mike's 'four or five years' is written 'most of three years'; 'first time since 1948' is not used. The index last ran above 60 in 2021 (64.7 in March 2021, the highest since 1983); copy says only 'above 60'. The 'needs above 60 for a parabolic run' and the 'slow grind above 50' are Mike's own thesis, in first person, and carry the deliberate engagement-bait one-liner.
fact_check.source: prnewswire.com/news-releases/manufacturing-pmi-at-54-5-september-2026-ism-manufacturing-pmi-report-302894520.html; fxstreet.com/news/us-ism-manufacturing-pmi-fell-to-545-in-september-202610011406; ismworld.org January 2026 PMI report (52.6); aa.com.tr/en/economy/us-manufacturing-sector-expands-for-1st-time-in-12-months-in-january/3818151; ftportfolios.com (ISM 64.7 in March 2021)

Citi raised its Strategy (MSTR) target to $240 from $136 (Buy) and its 12-month Bitcoin forecast to $113K from $82K. Red Octobers since 2013: 2014, 2018 and 2025 (three). Copy: 'CNBC is telling its audience Bitcoin is setting up for a big fourth quarter' (not 'massive bull market', not 'new all-time high soon'). yt_posts.body:
Bitcoin tagged $87K on the Oct 2 jobs report and gave the whole move back within hours. About $434M got liquidated in 24 hours, and roughly three quarters of it was longs.

That is a bull trap on the daily chart. Here is the question I keep coming back to: what if the whole market is setting one up for October?

Look at how fast the mood flipped. A few weeks ago the four-year cycle zombies were all waiting for an October bottom. That talk is gone. Now CNBC is telling its audience Bitcoin is setting up for a big fourth quarter, and the talking points are real:

1. Citi raised its price target on Strategy to $240 from $136, and its 12-month Bitcoin forecast to $113K from $82K.

2. There have only been three red Octobers since 2013: 2014, 2018 and 2025.

3. CryptoQuant shows whale stablecoin inflows to Binance up about 40% in a month, to $30.5B.

4. Jobs came in at 29K against about 90K expected, and prediction markets now price about an 82% chance the Fed holds rates on Oct 28.

All of that is bullish. And when everybody leans the same way, that is exactly how a trap gets set.

The scenario I am watching. Bitcoin ($BTC) opened October at about $83,555. It runs for another week or two, maybe to $90K, pulls everybody back in, then rolls over and closes the month below that open. That is a red October, the opposite of what everybody is pricing in.

Notice where the money is going too. The total crypto market crossed $3 trillion in late September, but the money is flowing into the top 100. Mid caps, low caps and micro caps are bleeding out.

I am not turning bearish. Bitcoin has two weekly closes above the 50-week SMA and it is above the May high, so for me the bull market is official. The low near $58K this summer was the bottom. We are not going back there, and forget $40K. A red October would be a pullback inside a bull market.

But parabolic? Not yet. ISM Manufacturing PMI printed 54.5 for September. It spent most of three years under 50, broke out in January, and has been grinding sideways above it for nine straight months instead of shooting up. We need that number above 60 before I start talking about a parabolic run.

So bet right now, in the comments: does Bitcoin close October above or below $83,555?
